---
title: "Colours and themes"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 7,
  fig.height = 4.2,
  dpi = 72,
  out.width = "100%"
)
```

```{r}
library(plot2)
```

This article describes how `plot2()` sets colours, how to use palettes and the colours of an organisation, and how to change the theme and the titles of a plot.

## Setting colours

`colour` sets the colours of a plot, whatever its type. `ggplot2` distinguishes between the `colour` aesthetic (for points and lines) and the `fill` aesthetic (for areas such as bars), each with its own scale functions. `plot2()` determines which of the two applies and sets both where needed. Without `colour`, the colours of `ggplot2` are used:

```{r}
admitted_patients |>
  plot2(x = hospital, y = n(), category = ward)
```

`colour` accepts R colour names, hexadecimal codes and palette names. A vector of colours is used in the order of the values of `category`:

```{r}
admitted_patients |>
  plot2(x = hospital, y = n(), category = ward, colour = c("steelblue", "#E15759"))
```

A named vector matches its names to the values of `category`, so that a value keeps its colour in every plot, even when not all values are present:

```{r}
admitted_patients |>
  plot2(x = hospital,
        y = n(),
        category = ward,
        colour = c("Non-ICU" = "grey70", "ICU" = "#E15759"))
```

### Palettes

The colourblind-safe palettes of the `viridisLite` package are available by name: `"viridis"`, `"magma"`, `"inferno"`, `"plasma"`, `"cividis"`, `"rocket"`, `"mako"` and `"turbo"`. So are the palettes of base R, such as `"Okabe-Ito"`, `"R4"` and `"Tableau 10"` (see `grDevices::palette.pals()`):

```{r}
admitted_patients |>
  plot2(x = age_group, y = n(), category = hospital, colour = "Tableau 10")
```

`get_colour()` returns the colours that `plot2()` uses for a name or palette. A palette is extended where needed, so that it never runs out of colours:

```{r}
get_colour("Tableau 10", length = 4)
get_colour(c("red", "#4E79A7", "f80"))
```

### Colour and fill

Where a geom has both a line and an area, such as columns and boxplots, `colour` applies to both. `colour_fill` sets the area separately:

```{r}
admitted_patients |>
  plot2(x = hospital,
        y = age,
        category = ward,
        type = "boxplot",
        colour = c("#4E79A7", "#E15759"),
        colour_fill = "white")
```

`colour_transparency` makes the colours transparent, from 0 (solid) to 1 (fully transparent).

### Numeric categories

A numeric `category` gets a continuous colour scale. Two colours give a gradient, and three colours give a scale that diverges from the midpoint, which `category.midpoint` sets:

```{r}
mtcars |>
  plot2(x = wt,
        y = mpg,
        category = hp,
        colour = c("#2166AC", "grey90", "#B2182B"),
        category.midpoint = 150,
        size = 3)
```

### Highlighting a value

`category.focus` shows one value in its colour and the other values in grey. It accepts a value or its position:

```{r}
admitted_patients |>
  plot2(x = format(date, "%Y"),
        y = n(),
        category = hospital,
        category.focus = "D",
        type = "line",
        x.title = "Year")
```

## Colours of an organisation

`register_colour()` adds colours under a name of your choice, which can then be used everywhere `plot2()` accepts colours. A set of registered colours can itself be registered as a palette:

```{r}
register_colour(company_blue = "#1F3A93",
                company_orange = "#D35400",
                company_green = "#2C6F47",
                company_grey = "#708090")
register_colour(company = c("company_blue", "company_orange", "company_green", "company_grey"))

get_colour("company", length = 4)
```

```{r}
admitted_patients |>
  plot2(x = age_group, y = n(), category = hospital, colour = "company")
```

The option `plot2.colour` sets the default colours for all plots in the session:

```{r}
options(plot2.colour = "company")

admitted_patients |>
  plot2(x = hospital, y = n(), category = gender)
```

```{r}
options(plot2.colour = NULL)
unregister_colour("^company")
```

A package can register colours when it is loaded, so that all users of that package get the same colours. `?get_colour` shows how.

## Themes

`plot2()` applies `theme_minimal2()` by default. This theme is based on `ggplot2::theme_minimal()`, with fewer grid lines, more white space and the legend at the top, and it is suited to print. The `theme` argument sets another theme, and `theme = NULL` uses the default theme of `ggplot2`:

```{r}
admitted_patients |>
  plot2(x = hospital, y = n(), theme = ggplot2::theme_bw())
```

A partial theme, made with `ggplot2::theme()`, is added to `theme_minimal2()`, so that only the given elements change:

```{r}
admitted_patients |>
  plot2(x = hospital,
        y = n(),
        theme = ggplot2::theme(panel.grid.major.y = ggplot2::element_blank()))
```

Other arguments change frequent elements directly. `background` sets the background colour, `text_factor` scales all text, and `legend.position` places the legend:

```{r}
admitted_patients |>
  plot2(x = hospital,
        y = n(),
        category = gender,
        background = "#F5F5F0",
        text_factor = 1.2,
        legend.position = "right")
```

The options `plot2.theme`, `plot2.colour_background`, `plot2.text_factor`, `plot2.colour_font_primary` (title), `plot2.colour_font_secondary` (subtitle and caption) and `plot2.colour_font_axis` (axis titles) set these defaults for all plots. `?plot2-options` lists all options.

## Titles

Titles support markdown for italic (`*text*`) and bold (`**text**`) text, which is often needed for the names of species, and `<br>` for a line break. `plot2()` converts the markdown to a `plotmath` expression with `md_to_expression()`:

```{r}
data.frame(species = c("E. coli", "K. pneumoniae", "S. aureus"),
           isolates = c(412, 128, 197)) |>
  plot2(x = species,
        y = isolates,
        title = "Isolates of *E. coli*, *K. pneumoniae* and *S. aureus*",
        subtitle = "**Fictitious** data",
        x.label_italic = TRUE)
```

Set `markdown = FALSE` to show the text as it is. Long titles are wrapped at `title.linelength` characters.
